newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea to sell 9.65 mln shrs of Korea Teleco.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to sell 9.65 mln shrs of Korea Teleco.

text.p: The South Korean government plans to sell 9.65 million shares, valued at about 360 billion won, of state-backed telephone service provider Korea Telecom in an auction on November 28 and 29, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
The ministry said in a statement the company would be listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in the first half of 1997.
The ministry said the auction represents 3.35 percent of the telephone service provider's outstanding shares. An additional 3.32 million shares would be sold to Korea Telecom employees as scheduled.
The minimum bid was set at 37,600 won per share.
Individual investors as well as corporations will be eligible to bid in the auction, which is being managed by Kookmin Bank.
Successful purchasers will be announced on December 4. There is no maximum limit set for the number of shares that can be bid for, but each bid must be for more than 50 shares, it said.
Previous Korea Telecom share auctions, offered only to institutional investors and corporations, were undersubscribed in a depressed stock market.
The ministry said it may sell the shares overseas after listing in the local market.
Korea Telecom has a monopoly on South Korea's local telephone service, and holds the lion's share of the long distance and data communications markets.
